text:
mia: FYI deploy-bot suggested backporting the auth token rotation fix as a minor to 1.x, 2.x and main. It looks like a behavior change for some token consumers; I'd prefer patch cherrypick for 2.x and patch for main, but 1.x should be left alone unless we explicitly support it.

release-bot: backport analysis: PR#3590 touches: src/auth/*, docs/api.md. Heuristic: auth API edits -> candidate minor for all tracked branches. Suggested branches: main, v2.x, v1.x. Backport confidence: medium.

owen: If it changes token expiry semantics, that's a behavioral change. But if it's only rotations behind the scenes, we shouldn't force minors. We need a checklist: does public request/response change? If no -> patch.

chris: Ops: during the maintenance window we try to avoid cross-branch minors. Patches only. We can do a targeted minor later in a release cycle if customers need new behavior.

mia: Agreed. I'll run the cherrypick with --patch-only to main and v2.x. For v1.x we'll open a support ticket and ask if customers want the change.

release-bot: action: created candidate tags -> main:v3.2.5-patch, v2.x:v2.9.8-patch. Backport PRs opened: #3590-backport-main, #3590-backport-v2.x. Annotated with: "reason: auth rotation - internal semantics; forced patch by author".

ops: quick note: ensure release-notes generator doesn't auto-promote backports to 'Feature' section. Use frontmatter `semver: patch` in backport PR body.

owen: tiny upstream ask: can deploy-bot add a "backport-recommendation" field explaining risk (none/low/medium/high) so reviewers know whether to escalate to product?

release-bot: enhancement logged: rfc/semver-backport-guidelines #7. Will attach risk score based on number of API files touched and exported symbol diffs.

mia: Posting to #release-notes: "v3.2.5 (patch) - auth token rotation bugfix; cherrypicked from main; no API contract changes" :white_check_mark:

chris: Thanks. Filing follow-up RFC to tighten backport heuristics and to add gating: cross-branch minors require approval from release-approvers.

mia: Closing thread. Thanks all.
